title: Alpha and Omega's Huawei power-semiconductor settlement records samples, in-country transfers, a business-unit exit, and conditional export privileges
source_unit: BIS June 27, 2025 final order and July 2, 2025 announcement for Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Incorporated
geography: United States, Taiwan-linked and PRC operations, Huawei, and power-semiconductor supply chains

observations.period: May 28 through November 22, 2019 conduct; final BIS order June 27, 2025

denominator.unit: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Incorporated administrative settlement

company_and_product.value: AOS designs, develops, and supplies power semiconductors; the order concerns power controllers, smart power stages, and related accessories

huawei_entity_list_date.unit: date Huawei and listed non-U.S. affiliates were added to the Entity List

unauthorized_occurrences.unit: occasions on which AOS forwarded items from the United States without BIS authorization

items_forwarded.unit: approximately power controllers, smart power stages, and related accessories

transfer_structure.value: items were exported to an AOS facility in China and AOS believes its employees there transferred them to Huawei; four occasions involved approximately 600 items and eleven involved approximately 1,056 items
transfer_structure.unit: reported export and in-country transfer route

civil_penalty.unit: U.S. dollars; civil penalty ordered by BIS

payment_condition.value: full and timely payment was made a condition to granting, restoring, or continuing export licenses, license exceptions, permissions, or privileges; nonpayment could lead to one year of export-privilege denial

business_unit_outcome.value: the Digital Power business unit was eliminated in 2021 because it never generated significant revenue

production_or_capability_effect.unit: missing Huawei product qualification, downstream use, production, revenue, worker, or capability endpoint

strategic_effect.unit: missing deterrence, substitution, PRC response, partner response, or U.S. leverage

observations.method: BIS final-order and official announcement review. The order's admitted conduct, item count, transfer route, penalty, export-privilege condition, and separately reported business-unit outcome are coded as distinct stages; the business-unit elimination is not attributed causally to the enforcement action.
observations.uncertainty: The order reports approximate item counts and states that AOS believed China-based employees transferred the items to Huawei; it does not establish Huawei's testing result, commercial qualification, final use, or production effect. The 2021 business-unit elimination is temporally later but the source does not attribute its cause to the violations or settlement.
observations.subgroup: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor, its Digital Power business unit and China affiliate, Huawei, export-control counsel and staff, U.S. authorities, and power-semiconductor customers
observations.counterinterpretation: A conditional export-privilege remedy may improve compliance incentives without changing product demand or foreign capability. The business-unit elimination may reflect commercial underperformance rather than enforcement, and this single order does not establish a general relationship between export controls and firm exit.

related_sources.claim: BIS final order and settlement text for Alpha and Omega Semiconductor, including the fifteen charges, approximately 1,650 items, penalty, conditional export privileges, and business-unit statement.
Related named semiconductor-equipment enforcement case for comparison of penalty, compliance obligations, and China route.
Related named semiconductor-design-tool enforcement case for comparison of entity-list routing and remediation.

boundary: This record adds a power-semiconductor enforcement route: Entity List addition -> sample and in-country transfer route -> civil penalty -> conditional export privileges, alongside a temporally later but non-causally attributed business-unit elimination. It does not establish Huawei capability change, future compliance, deterrence, or geopolitical leverage.
